🖥 Iran backs initiatives promoting peace, multilateralism, international law: FM spokesperson

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei says Tehran supports any initiative that promotes international peace and security, multilateralism, the UN Charter and international law.

During a weekly press conference on Tuesday, Baqaei described China as a friend and a vital trading and strategic partner, emphasizing Beijing’s role in promoting multilateralism and fostering solidarity among countries in the Global South.
​
Baqaei also attributed the region’s severe insecurity over the past year to the illegal actions of the US and the Israeli regime, noting that the only way to resolve the issues created by the US is to change course as soon as possible and to avoid becoming further embroiled in crisis.
​
Regarding Syria, Baqaei said that Iran had not sent any message indicating a desire to establish relations with Syria. He emphasized that Iran’s past support for Syria was given at the request of its then-legitimate government to fight terrorism and maintain the country’s territorial integrity.
​
He also condemned the Israeli regime’s occupation of parts of Syria’s Golan Heights and its ongoing actions against Syria, reiterating Iran’s firm opposition to such measures.
​
Elsewhere in his remarks, Baqaei referred to the trilateral Turkiye-Pakistan-Saudi security pact, adding that Iran does not view the arrangement as a threat and believes regional Muslim countries are turning to mutual cooperation to safeguard their security.
​
He added that Iran is in dialogue with these countries and will continue consultations with Turkiye, an important neighbor with which Tehran has good relations, on all issues.
​
Baqaei urges Iraq, Kurdistan Region to curb terrorist activities against Iran
​
The spokesperson said that Iran continues to observe some terrorist groups exploiting regions in Iraq’s Kurdistan to plan and prepare actions against Iran. He emphasized the need for both Baghdad and the Kurdistan Region to enhance their efforts in fully implementing the security agreement and protecting border security.
​
He said that Iran has repeatedly raised these concerns with Iraqi and Kurdish officials and hopes the consultations will help eliminate security threats on both sides of the border.
​
FM spox slams EU for ignoring root causes of energy, economic crisis
​
Baqaei said that Iran hopes European countries will acknowledge that their fuel and economic problems stem from illegal US actions, but that they need moral courage to state this reality.
​
He described the EU statement as disappointing, saying Europe has chosen appeasement of the aggressor instead of addressing the root cause of the crisis, a policy he said would not work.
